text.p: European metal producer Metaleurop SA expects to post higher earnings in the 1996/97 financial year (October/September) than in 1995/96, its chairman Helmut Stodieck said on Tuesday.

In a presentation to the Association of Mining Analysts, Stodieck said net profits next year may rise to between 60 million and 200 million French francs, depending on the price of its two main products lead and zinc, and other factors.
"I see Metaleurop in the black (in 1996/97) and depending on market assumptions somewhere between 60 and 200 million French francs," he told reporters after the presentation.

The lower end of the band was based on an average zinc price over the period of $1,050 a tonne, an assumption which Stodieck called "conservative." The lead price assumption at the lower end of the band was $750.
"My personal view is that the markets have a higher potential," he said.
Prices of $1,300 for zinc and $850 for lead were used as the basis of the top end of the earnings expectations.
The exchange rate basis for both earning estimates was 5.17 French francs to the U.S. dollar.
For the 1995/96 financial year Stodieck said earnings were likely to be slightly below the half year net attributable profit figure of 52 million francs.
"The (full-year) figure may come a little below this for the full year because of the problems at our Nordenham (lead) smelter," he said.
Stodieck said the plant would only produce 55 percent of its 90,000-tonne annual capacity during its first full year of operations.
"We now have good reason to believe we have solved some of the major problems," Stodieck said.
